data.narrative:
Built Robotics, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Noah Ready-Campbell and Andrew Liang, has raised $112M+ to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), with primary focus on three same-sector, same-stage private companies: Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses total raised ($112M+) as a proxy base, applying a 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier to derive an implied valuation of $29M. Peer-median analysis across the three stage-matched comparables yields a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B. The peer set includes additional robotics companies (Divergent, Exotec) for broader context.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $25M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $514M. The wide dispersion reflects material tension between the stage-progression method—which produces a floor near $25M—and peer multiples, which cluster at or above $1.0B. Key uncertainties include whether Built Robotics' commercial traction, addressable market position, and capital efficiency justify peer-level valuations or suggest a discount to the median. Resolution of this gap requires granular assessment of revenue run-rate, unit economics, and competitive positioning relative to named peers.
